To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The join/leave conditions presented in Stoica et al., and Baruah, are sufficient for fair-scheduled multiprocssors, under any deadline based Pfair scheduling algorithm; (2) The join/leaves conditions presented for the PD^P2 Pfair algorithm are optimal, in the sense that they cannot be improved upon.

(i) for any deadline-based P-fair scheduling algorithm and any task utilization vector, the join/leave conditions of Stoica et al./Baruah et al., which were derived for uniprocessors, are also sufficient on multiprocessors, and (ii) for PD^2, the sufficient join/leave condition is tighter than the sufficient condition for uniprocessor PD^2.

(a) the conditions presented in Stoica et al.'s and Baruah's papers are sufficient for fair scheduling on multiprocessors, (b) PD^2 Pairs is the first deadline-based Pfair algorithm for which such conditions are known, and (c) the conditions for PD^2 Pair's are optimal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: "When can dynamic real-time task sets be scheduled in a fair way on multiprocessors?"
the question of whether dynamic task systems can be scheduled on multiprocessors in a fair manner.
the question of when dynamic task systems can be safely scheduled on multiprocessors, in such a way that no task ever misses its deadline.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a dynamic task system in which every subset of M - 1 tasks has total utilization of at most 1, the sufficient conditions for fair scheduling of the system on an M-processor system, under any deadlinebased Pfair scheduling algorithm (such as the Pfair, PD^2, and Pfair^2 algorithms), are the same as those for a uniprocessor system.
, for any Pfair algorithm, if the task system satisfies the sufficient join/leave condition for the PD^ 2 algorithm, then the system will be schedulable on any number of Pfair multiprocessors.

the join/leave conditions of Baruah et. al. for uniprocessors, and of the authors for multiprocessors, are necessary and sufficient for fair scheduling on uniprocessors and multiprocessors, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, on multiprocessors with PD^2 PFAIR scheduling, we can guarantee that no deadline will be missed, provided that the utilization of every set of M-1 jobs is no greater than M.

we provide sufficient join/leave fairness conditions for dynamic task systems on both uniprocessors and multiprocessors, and we prove that these conditions are tight in the sense that no less restrictive conditions guaranteeing join/leave fairness exist for the PD^ 2 Pfair algorithm.
we have provided sufficient conditions for fair-scheduling of dynamic task systems with arbitrary task utilizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of multiprocessors, fair scheduling of dynamic task sets is not significantly more difficult than fair scheduling of static task sets.

, while the scheduling of dynamic task sets is more difficult on a multiprocessor than on a single processor, there is a class of task sets for which it is possible to schedule the task set fairly without causing missed deadlines on a multiprocess.
fair scheduling of dynamic real-time systems is possible even in multiprocessors, as long as the task set utilizations are bounded.
